precepts.text: So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee.
precepts.point: Now the scriptures substantiate the vision Peter had. The vessel knit at the four corners is Israel, and the beasts within it are men. This is why the nations cannot handle us right now: when we speak, we can use the Bible to explain itself. When they hear it, they think it is everybody. No: God said Israel was the vessel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Another witness that the beasts in Peter's sheet are men: the psalmist says of himself, “So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee.”

A man, foolish and ignorant before God, is called a beast. So when Peter explained the vision to those of the circumcision who contended with him, he could say: remember, it is written in Psalms that we were as beasts before God.

That is the whole key to Acts 10. The fourfooted beasts in the vessel are not pork and shellfish made clean. They are the people of Israel who were foolish and ignorant, living as beasts before the Lord, whom God was now going to cleanse and gather back together.

precepts.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof.
precepts.point: When the Lord awakes and intervenes, he shall despise their image. That image is Cesare Borgia, the fake Jesus who represents all Edom.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
“Truly God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart”: to the twelve tribes, those who walk in righteousness and do the commandments. “But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped. For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.” Some of us in here get envious the same way when we see the prosperity of the wicked.

Who is the wicked? Job says: “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked”. If you don't know who the wicked is, it is telling you by a process of elimination. It ain't the black man and the Latin man; we are not ruling anything. We can't even rule our own homes. The white man rules supreme on this planet. You want anything done in your country, you have to go through that white man.

“he covereth the faces of the judges thereof”. The judges are God, Christ, the angels and the Israelites, and it is the white man who covers their faces. Look at the paintings: black Mary with a black baby Christ, and somehow that baby grows up and, Shazam, becomes a white man, and nobody sees anything wrong with that.

So the wicked whose prosperity Asaph envied is the one the earth has been given to for a time: the man who whitewashed the faces of the judges.

precepts.text: I hated Esau and laid his heritage waste, the Dark Ages. Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build: that is the Renaissance, when they returned and enslaved us. They shall build, but I will throw down, and men shall call them the border of wickedness, the people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.
precepts.point: When the Lord awakes and intervenes, he shall despise their image. That image is Cesare Borgia, the fake Jesus who represents all Edom.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Job 9:24 says the wicked has the earth. Malachi names him: “And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” That is the Dark Ages, when God made Esau poverty-stricken.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”. They returned in the time called the Renaissance, and that is when they conquered us and made us their slaves, Christian slaves. “thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down”. God said, I will give you a chance to build: they built up America, England, France, Germany, Australia, all those places they robbed and pillaged.

“and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Indignation means righteous anger, for ever. So it identifies who the wicked is: Esau, Edom.

That is why Asaph saw him prospering: wherever Esau goes, it seems whatever he touches turns to gold. But he is building only to be thrown down.

precepts.text: Deliver me from the evil man, preserve me from the violent man, which imagine mischiefs and are continually gathered together for war. If there is no war he will start one; it is his nature. Their tongues are sharpened like a serpent with adder's poison, and they hide snares, cords, nets and gins.
precepts.point: When the Lord awakes and intervenes, he shall despise their image. That image is Cesare Borgia, the fake Jesus who represents all Edom.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
“Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain; violence covereth them as a garment.” They have so much wealth that pride covers them like a chain, and much of their old slave money is invested in war companies, weaponry and the military. David names him: “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man”. This is about the white man. Preserve us from him.

“Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” If there is no war, you can bet your last dollar the white man will start one. He can never let there be peace on earth; the way God made him, it is his nature. Trump pledged to end global conflict and bombed at least seven countries in 2025; under Obama in 2016, 26,171 bombs were dropped on seven countries. And they took Maduro with weapons that shut his military down in minutes.

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips. Selah.” Selah means it is true. Whatever comes out of their mouth, religion or politics, is the worst kind of poison; for some of them politics is their religion. Take hold of it and you will die.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.” Their purpose on earth is to overthrow the twelve tribes of Israel. They can't rest if they see one of us in a nice car or a nice home: he must be selling drugs. “The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me.” The cords and the net are their traps of religion and politics, and a gin is a trap too. He is the wicked of Job 9:24 and Malachi 1, and he wears violence like he wears clothes.

precepts.text: Shall I count them pure with the wicked balances and the bag of deceitful weights? The rich men thereof are full of violence, and the inhabitants have spoken lies. The descendants justify their ancestors' evil because they benefit from it.
precepts.point: When the Lord awakes and intervenes, he shall despise their image. That image is Cesare Borgia, the fake Jesus who represents all Edom.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
“Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.” Read the top ten billionaires: Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, Bernard Arnault, Bill Gates, Mark Zuckerberg, and the rest. Zuckerberg stole Facebook from the college kids who hired him to create it. Micah asks: “Shall I count them pure with the wicked balances, and with the bag of deceitful weights?” Wicked balances are unjust judgments.

“For the rich men thereof are full of violence”. These rich people come from old money, gotten through the rape, robbery and pillaging of our nations and our people.

“and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.” Their descendants will say anything to justify the evil of their ancestors: it wasn't me, it was my ancestors, but I enjoy what they did. Why? Because they benefit from it.

That is what Asaph envied before he went into the sanctuary of God. Many times we envy people without knowing how they got their money, but nine times out of ten, especially with white folks, it came through criminality. Only by reading and understanding the word of God will you understand their end: set in slippery places and cast down into destruction.

precepts.text: His feet were almost gone when he was envious at the foolish and saw the prosperity of the wicked.
precepts.point: He asks the Most High to hold up his goings in his paths so that his footsteps slip not. Our footsteps slip when we come off the path of righteousness, turning to the right hand or the left instead of following the good path that leads to the kingdom.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
David asks the Most High to “Hold up my goings in thy paths, that my footsteps slip not.” Here he shows what it looks like when the feet start to slip: “But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped.”

And he tells why: “For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.” Envy at the foolish, looking at the prosperity of the wicked, is what nearly took his feet out from under him.

Our footsteps slip when we come off the path of righteousness, turning to the right hand or the left instead of following the good path that leads to the kingdom. Envy at the wicked is one of the things that pulls us off that path.

precepts.text: Not until he went into the sanctuary of the Most High did he understand their end; get knowledge and understanding built up first.
precepts.point: He asks the Most High to hold up his goings in his paths so that his footsteps slip not. Our footsteps slip when we come off the path of righteousness, turning to the right hand or the left instead of following the good path that leads to the kingdom.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
David's feet were almost gone when he envied the wicked, and he tells what turned it: “Until I went into the sanctuary of God; then understood I their end.” Not until he went into the sanctuary of the Most High did he understand where the wicked and their prosperity end up.

That is how the Most High holds up our goings in his paths: get knowledge and understanding built up first. With understanding of their end, the prosperity of the wicked no longer pulls the feet off the path.

precepts.text: I was envious at the foolish when I saw the prosperity of the wicked, for there are no bands in their death and their strength is firm; pride and violence cover them.
precepts.point: Do not fret because of evildoers nor be envious against the workers of iniquity, for they shall soon be cut down like the grass.

note.label: Psalm 37: Fret Not Because of Evildoers

precepts.why:
“Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.” The psalmist confesses the very thing: “For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.” Read on and he says why it looked so good: there are no bands in their death and their strength is firm; pride and violence cover them.

This chapter hit home. Coming into this truth, David saw where his life was versus where other people's lives were and what they were doing, and it started to mess with his spirit a little. When I first came into the truth I would look at the wicked of our people and of the other nations, with no God and no laws, and they were prospering with a bunch of material things. That is why the scripture says do not fret or be envious of them: “they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb.” Reading things like this gave the strength to keep going.

precepts.text: Behold, these are the ungodly who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.
precepts.point: Man being in honor abides not; he is like the beasts that perish, boasting himself and naming things after himself but destined to die.

note.label: Psalm 49: The Vanity of Riches Against the Grave

precepts.why:
“Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.” The ones prospering and increasing in riches are the ungodly, the same ones in Psalm 49 who leave their wealth to others and call their lands after their own names. Their prosperity is not the blessing of the Most High; it comes from the one who said the power and glory of the world were delivered unto him.

Wise men die, and the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others. A rich man dying without a will leaves Esau to take his money and pay his own people with it. The ungodly boast themselves and name things after themselves, but they are destined to die like the beasts.

precepts.text: Two types of people: those that are full deny the Most High and say who is the Lord, and those with too little steal and take His name in vain.
precepts.point: They set their mouth against the heavens and their tongue walks through the earth.

note.label: Psalm 73: God Is Good to Israel

precepts.why:
Psalm 73 describes the wicked who prosper: “Their eyes stand out with fatness: they have more than heart could wish.” They have abundance, more than they need, and “pride compasseth them about as a chain”. They wear their pride because they think no hurt can come to them. The entertainers, rappers and people in Congress live luxurious lives and no harm comes to them.

Proverbs shows why that fatness is dangerous: “Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.”

Two types of people: those that are full deny the Most High and say who is the Lord, and those with too little steal and take his name in vain. The full ones are the ones of Psalm 73 who “set their mouth against the heavens” and “speak wickedly concerning oppression”, speaking loftily and proudly. Our people do not believe they are oppressed; some say there is no racism and the world is equal. Better to be fed with food convenient for you than to be so full you deny the Lord.

precepts.text: We must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.
precepts.point: The Most High shall guide him with His counsel and afterward receive him to glory.

note.label: Psalm 73: God Is Good to Israel

precepts.why:
The psalmist says, “Thus my heart was grieved, and I was pricked in my reins. So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee.” He was grieved watching the wicked prosper. “Nevertheless I am continually with thee: thou hast holden me by my right hand.” He snapped back to his senses and realized the wicked are set for destruction.

Paul and Barnabas taught the same, “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” Those afflicted are being prepared. We must go through much afflictions to enter the kingdom, whether financial, spiritual, physical or mental.

So the grief and the affliction are not a sign that the Most High has left. He holds us by the right hand through it, and “Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.” The tribulation is the road into the kingdom.

precepts.text: Paul asked three times for his infirmity removed, but the Most High said His grace was sufficient and His strength made perfect in weakness.
precepts.point: It is good to draw near to God; he puts his trust in the Lord God that he may declare all His works.

note.label: Psalm 73: God Is Good to Israel

precepts.why:
“My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.” We all go through hard times, but we come back and understand the Most High is the strength of our heart and flesh. Paul lived this: “there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.”

Paul asked three times for his infirmity to be removed, but the Most High said, “My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.” So Paul says, “Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.”

That is what it means for God to be the strength of your heart when your flesh fails. The weakness stays, and his strength is made perfect in it. Whom have we in heaven but him, and there is none upon earth we desire beside him, so “it is good for me to draw near to God”.

precepts.text: The ungodly prosper, but when I went into the sanctuary of God then understood I their end.
precepts.point: The Most High cast us off among the heathen and scattered us among the countries, yet he became to us a little sanctuary in the countries where we come. In these sanctuaries you learn who the ungodly are, who prosper in this world serving Satan, and what their end is.

note.label: Psalm 134: The Servants Blessing the Most High in the Sanctuary

precepts.why: “Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.” It was too painful to understand, “Until I went into the sanctuary of God; then understood I their end.” In the sanctuary, where we lift up our hands and bless the Most High, you learn who the ungodly are, who prosper in this world serving Satan, and what their end is.
